From: Julia Park <julia@borealishealth.com>

Cc: security@borealishealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify cloud carve-out segmentation and KMS custody for SOC 2 scope

Hi Ava —

We're preparing for our SOC 2 Type II vendor review and have a couple of carve-out / subservice questions for Redwood that we need resolved before our auditor's kickoff (audit kickoff targeted for 2026-09-15). High level items we need: 

1) Clear delineation of responsibilities between Redwood and cloud providers (compute/storage/network) — do you treat the cloud provider as a subservice organization whose SOC 2 report we should include, or do you provide a bridge letter / carve-out statement?

2) KMS / key custody: Borealis runs in Dedicated capacity; our security team needs documented evidence of key ownership and custody model for that deployment mode (customer-managed CMKs vs Redwood-managed). Specifically: any logs or attestations showing key creation/rotation and whether Redwood has any direct access to plaintext keys.

3) Subprocessor list and evidence of coverage in provider reports (we need to know which subprocessors are within scope versus outside).

Can you provide: Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II (or relevant extracts), a template or sample bridge letter you can sign for our audit period (Jan 1–Jun 30, 2026), and any redacted KMS rotation/attestation records suitable for external review? Please also confirm whether you will accept a cloud provider SOC2 report (e.g., AWS/GCP) as coverage for underlying infrastructure or if you will provide a carve-out/bridge approach.

Deadline: if possible we'd like these artifacts by 2026-09-06 to share with our auditor.

Thanks — looking forward to your guidance.

Best,
Julia Park
Security & Privacy Lead
Borealis Health

Subject: Re: Clarify cloud carve-out segmentation and KMS custody for SOC 2 scope

Julia —

Thanks for the clear list and deadline. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

- Provider SOC 2: Redwood treats the cloud provider as a subservice organization. For hosted deployments we rely on provider SOC reports for underlying infrastructure; for Dedicated we can provide either (a) evidence linking provider SOC coverage + our bridge letter, or (b) a combined subservice mapping that shows which controls we assume versus which are delegated to the cloud provider. We typically provide a bridge letter that ties our SOC coverage window to the provider's report when audits overlap.

- KMS custody: For Dedicated capacity customers who choose customer-managed KMS, Borealis controls the CMKs and Redwood does not have access to plaintext keys. For hosted customers we manage keys via our HSM-backed KMS; in that case Redwood holds key custody under strict controls. We can provide a redacted key-rotation summary and HSM attestation for hosted flows; for Dedicated (customer-managed) we can provide a responsibility matrix and logs showing we have never accessed the CMKs.

- Subprocessors: we'll provide a current subprocessor list and call out which subprocessors are covered by provider SOC 2 vs those covered by Redwood SOC 2.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I will loop in Rishi (Security) and Marcus (Operations) to prepare the artifacts you requested (SOC extracts, bridge-letter draft, redacted KMS rotation summary).
2) Can you confirm whether Borealis is running Dedicated with customer-managed KMS (per your note) — that will determine the KMS evidence we provide.
3) If your auditor needs a call, let's schedule a 30-minute sync the week of 9/7.

We can target delivery of preliminary artifacts by 2026-09-03 if you confirm Dedicated + CMK ownership; final bridge letter by 9/06. If your auditor insists on provider SOC reports covering the exact audit window, we'll include the underlying provider report excerpts and our mapping.

Attaching a quick mapping template to capture what your auditor typically needs.

Best,
Ava Chen
Head of Solutions — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
